taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Kenpoly-convocation-arena, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1434 | 2.5 | 2.5
2 | 1879 | 5.42 | 7.92
3 | 318 | 18 | 25.9
4 | 3488 | 24.3 | 50.2
5 | 542 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as A-type.

Is this label correct for these layer values? Give a short answer, then end with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"label_correct": true or false, "curve_type": "<letters>"}

No, the label is incorrect. Based on the resistivity values provided, the curve type is determined by comparing consecutive groups of three layers:
- **Layers 1-2-3**: 1434 < 1879 > 318 (Pattern K: $r_1 < r_2 > r_3$)
- **Layers 2-3-4**: 1879 > 318 < 3488 (Pattern H: $r_1 > r_2 < r_3$)
- **Layers 3-4-5**: 318 < 3488 > 542 (Pattern K: $r_1 < r_2 > r_3$)

The resulting sequence of letters is **KHK**. An A-type curve would require the resistivity to be strictly increasing across all layers ($\rho_1 < \rho_2 < \rho_3 < \rho_4 < \rho_5$).

{"label_correct": false, "curve_type": "KHK"}
